tagline.text: The northwestern gateway port of Bohol, reached by sea from Cebu

location.label: Location
location.text: Northwestern coast of Bohol, a port town on the Cebu Strait (about 54 km north of Tagbilaran)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱700~2,500 (per person, based on a round-trip day trip from Cebu including ferry, local transport and meals)

children.text: Tubigon is a port town on Bohol's northwestern coast and the Bohol port closest to Cebu City. With Ilijan Hill Nature Park, known as the Philippines' first volcanic plug, the mangroves and bat watching on Cabgan Island, and around 17 small islands offshore, it is worth more than a quick transfer.

Tubigon is a municipality on the northwestern coast of Bohol Island. It borders Calape to the west, Clarin to the east and San Isidro to the south, with the Cebu Strait to the north. According to Wikipedia its area is 81.87 square kilometers, its 2024 population is 49,275 and it has 34 barangays. It lies about 54 km north of Tagbilaran, Bohol's main city, and the national road is paved, so the drive takes about 1 hour. The municipality is classed as first-class in income, farming and fishing are the main industries, and about 60 percent of the land is agricultural. Rice, corn, coconut, bananas and vegetables are grown, and the town is also known for its "lambay" crabs.

Above all, Tubigon is the closest port for entering Bohol from Cebu. It is described as Bohol's second-largest port, with about 20 scheduled trips a day to Cebu City (6 conventional vessels and 2 fastcraft), and a roll-on, roll-off ferry is said to make two trips daily. For that reason many travelers enter through Tubigon instead of Tagbilaran and take a bus or van south toward Panglao. The FastCat terminal is said to be in Barangay Oriental, beside the Tubigon Cultural Center. If your timing allows, rather than heading south right after arriving, it is worth spending half a day in town.

One account says the name comes from the frequent flooding here, and the first settlers are thought to have crossed from Southeast Asia in outrigger bangkas. The first written records appear in the early 17th century. In 1816 it was organized as a visita (dependent village) of Calape, and in 1819 it became an independent town, with Matong as its first gobernadorcillo. On February 9, 1852 a parish was established under San Isidro Labrador (St. Isidore the Farmer), with Fray Pedro Polo del Carmen as the first parish priest. There was a boundary dispute with neighboring Calape in 1852–1856, and a compromise line ratified on September 18, 1856 was marked with stone monuments. On January 31, 1919 five barrios were separated to form Clarin. The parish feast day is May 15. In the 2013 Bohol earthquake the town church and town hall were totally destroyed, and the quake is recorded as killing 11 people and damaging about 7,300 homes. Check locally for how things look after reconstruction.

Tubigon's attractions fall into three groups. First is the Enchanted Ilijan Hill volcanic plug nature park in the poblacion (town center), which PHIVOLCS is said to have certified as the Philippines' first volcanic plug. On April 15, 2024 Tubigon received ₱25 million from the Department of Tourism's Tourism Champions Challenge for five years of development, and a visitor center, view deck, Ilijan Heritage Center, an arts and culture village and a garden trail are planned or under construction. Second are the roughly 17 small islands scattered offshore. Bagongbanwa, Batasan, Bilangbilangan, Mocaboc, Pangapasan and Ubay Island and Reef are among those listed, and since there are no scheduled boats you must charter a bangka. Third is the mangrove walk and bat watching on Cabgan Island, for which the Bohol tourism site advises booking at least 2 days ahead. Tubigon loomweaving and the Macaas Boardwalk also appear on travel sites, but little detail is available.

blocks.title: Ilijan Hill volcanic plug nature park

children.text: A hill introduced as the Philippines' first volcanic plug, right in the middle of the town center. A visitor center, view deck, heritage center and garden trail are planned, so what is open varies over time. Check with the tourism office before you visit.
The main port of northwestern Bohol, where boats to and from Cebu arrive and depart. The FastCat terminal is next to the Cultural Center. Keep an eye on your belongings in a busy port.
The parish church dedicated to St. Isidore the Farmer. It was heavily destroyed in the 2013 earthquake and reconstruction has followed. The town is liveliest around the feast day of May 15.

blocks.title: Cabgan Island mangroves and bat watching

children.text: A mangrove walkway and bat watching tour are listed on the Bohol tourism site. Booking is required at least
2 days
ahead, so a same-day visit is difficult.

Offshore from Tubigon there are about 17 small islands, including Bagongbanwa, Batasan and Pangapasan. There are no scheduled boats, so you charter a bangka. Check the price and safety gear before departure.

blocks.title: Lambay crab and the local market

children.text: Tubigon is known for lambay crab. At the market and seafood restaurants you can try freshly caught crab and fish. Prices are by market rate, so ask first.
Travel sites list a weaving craft experience. Ask the local tourism office whether it is available and what it costs.

items.title: Day trip from Cebu
items.subtitle: Cross by ferry and see the town and the mangroves

children.text: Board the ferry to Tubigon at Cebu City Pier 3. Depending on the operator and trip it takes about 1 to 2 hours.
Arrive at Tubigon port, pay the terminal fee and head into town.
Walk around Ilijan Hill and the town church area.
Have lunch near the market and try the seafood.
If you have booked ahead, set out on the Cabgan Island mangrove and bat watching tour.
Take the ferry back to Cebu from the port. Check the time of the last trip in advance.
Ferry times differ by operator and are sometimes cancelled because of weather. For a same-day round trip, check the last departure first.

items.title: Bohol transfer route
items.subtitle: Arrive in Tubigon and continue toward Panglao

children.text: Arrive in Tubigon by ferry from Cebu.
Take a bus or van to Tagbilaran from in front of the port. Buses are said to run about every 30 minutes.
Change at Tagbilaran for Panglao or your other destination.
The road from Tubigon to Tagbilaran is paved and takes about 1 hour. Some guides say this route can be cheaper and faster than a direct ferry to Tagbilaran.
Fly from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), travel to the pier in Cebu City, and board the ferry.
Tubigon is the closest Bohol port to Cebu City. For the trip from the airport to the pier, use a taxi or a ride-hailing car.

Get around town by tricycle, and ask the fare before you get in.
Tubigon is best for sea trips in the dry season from December to May. Bohol's typhoon season is described as September to February, with occasional typhoons from March to August.

According to modeled climate data, annual rainfall is about 1,326 mm, with April the driest month (about 71 mm). Rain is heaviest in October and November (about 174 mm in November). Average daily highs are 28–31°C and lows are 23–24°C.

Tubigon has small guesthouses and homestays around the port and in town, but reliable up-to-date information on prices and facilities is limited. Most travelers transfer on and stay in Panglao or Tagbilaran. If you plan to do the Ilijan Hill or Cabgan Island tours, it is better to book your lodging in advance.

From Tubigon, roads lead inland to Catigbian and San Isidro, so with a rented car you can link up with inland Bohol towns. However, public transport is easiest toward Tagbilaran, and it is more accurate to ask locally about inland routes and fares. Some guides say the Cebu–Tubigon route carries only foot passengers, while others say RORO car ferries also run, so ask the operator first if you want to take a vehicle across.

The lambay crab is the town's signature food. You can try it grilled or steamed at the seafood section of the market and at restaurants near the port. It is sold at market price, so confirm the weight and price first. Simple snacks are also available from stalls around the ferry terminal.
Check ferry schedules and fares directly with the operators' websites or by phone. They change from time to time.
According to the Bohol tourism site, tours of Cabgan Island must be booked at least 2 days ahead.
Some guides say going to Panglao via Tubigon can be cheaper and faster than a direct ferry to Tagbilaran.
There are no scheduled boats to the islands, so agree on a price and check whether life jackets are provided.
Ilijan Hill Nature Park is still being developed, and the areas that are open may change. Check before you visit.
At the port, keep your bags on you and spread your cash around.
Typhoons and high waves can delay or cancel ferries. Leave some slack in your schedule the day before your flight home.
The area was hit by the 2013 Bohol earthquake, so check the state of reconstruction of buildings locally.
Bangkas for island tours do not run on a schedule. Check the safety gear and cancel if the weather is bad.
Ferry fares and times change a lot with the season. The values here are approximate.
For bat watching on Cabgan Island, follow your guide under the conservation rules, and avoid loud noise and flash photography.
